title: Precision and Fisher-Test Resolution Tradeoff for Blocking Few Clusters under Score Error
banked_reason: Cold tier incremental; paper-score ceiling 5.6 below field threshold 7.4; salvageable false.
gap_reasons: The promised calibrated design implications are not delivered: the node supplies only a conditional δ≥ε+κ/2 implication for externally supplied uniform bounds, with no calibration procedure, validation-data/transport specification, or defensible radius; supply one or explicitly narrow the recorded promise.

The central positioning omits the listed Kapelner--Krieger--Azriel (Stat 2025) comparator, whose abstract proves asymptotic pairwise-matching optimality among blocking designs under a simultaneous-tail criterion; it does not evidently subsume this finite common-box frontier, but related_work and the comparator table must state that scope distinction.

The exact contribution is mathematically valid but remains a narrow product-stratified sensitivity analysis; its arbitrary-score result is a certificate rather than a structural frontier, its explicit noncontiguous gain is below 0.5%, and neither defensible radii nor material design evidence can be supplied without new data-generating and transport assumptions.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the exact finite-population risk and support laws, nominal contiguity, common-box block costs, an eight-cluster noncontiguity phase, polynomial arbitrary-score certificates, and a sharp full-block threshold. The mathematics passed, but the cold review rated the package incremental: the explicit gain is below 0.5%, the arbitrary-score result is only a certificate, and calibrated radii require a new validation/transport model.
tldr: For a few-cluster trial, we characterize the exact precision and Fisher-resolution tradeoff within independently randomized, half-treated even blocks under a common score-error box. Nominal score order suffices, but an exact eight-cluster \(5\%\) phase has a strictly better noncontiguous robust design. We give exact subset and prefix certificates, grid and perturbation conditions for safe ordered blocking, and a sharp universal full-block radius elbow of order \(nL\), where \(L\) is score range. The result concerns the product-stratified design class and a sensitivity radius that needs external justification.
gap: Known-score pairing and a general minimax atom-cap program do not characterize the restricted product-block frontier under a common score box. An exact eight-cluster witness shows robust contiguity fails, but general score-dependent conditions and practical radius calibration remain open.
fill: Prove the nominal profile rules and box-cost reduction, develop structural or economical exact certificates for irregular-score robust phases, and report sensitivity analyses only for externally defensible radius ranges.
